newsitem.title: JAPAN: Chip slip to hurt Japan electronics firms' profits.
newsitem.headline: Chip slip to hurt Japan electronics firms' profits.

text.p: Tumbling chip prices are thought to have hurt Japanese electronics firms' profits in the first half of this business year, although strong sales of communications products will ease the pain, analysts say.

"All the firms will be hit hard by lower chip prices, though strong sales in the communications sector will make up for some losses at some firms," said analyst Hiroyuki Horii of Yamaichi Research Institute of Securities and Economics.

Parent results for the six months to September 30 will be unveiled on October 25 by Japan's five biggest semiconductor makers -- NEC Corp, Toshiba Corp, Hitachi Ltd, Fujitsu Ltd and Mitsubishi Electric Corp. NEC will announce group results on October 25 and Toshiba on October 29.

While all rely heavily on their semiconductor business, the dependency is seen as particularly high at Toshiba and NEC, where the chip business accounts for 65 to 75 percent of their parent current profit, according to one analyst.
Amid a supply glut, prices of 16-megabit dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips, the mainstay for personal computers, have plunged over 70 percent in the past 10 months.
The falls in chip prices appear to have halted in early October, after makers curtailed supplies, analysts said.
Horii expects Toshiba's parent current profit for first half of 1996/97 to have fallen to 18 billion yen ($162 million), little more than half the previous year's figure.
Current profit is pretax, and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities such as investment in stocks.
NEC is expected to barely maintain its year-earlier profit levels by posting 30 billion yen ($270 million), helped by a strong showing in its communications division, Horii said.
Mami Indo, analyst at Daiwa Institute of Research, expects both NEC and Toshiba to post parent current profit of 35 billion yen ($315 million) in the first half of 1996/97.
"A plunge in memory chip prices, particularly since May, will show its full impact in the second half," Indo said.
Analysts are also watching to see if the firms revise full-year forecasts when they give mid-term results this month.

Hitachi, which is relatively weak in the communications equipment sector, announced earlier this month that it was cutting its full-year parent current forecast to 70 billion yen ($630 million) from 110 billion yen ($990 million). The new forecast represents a 46 percent drop from year-ago levels.
